cars.specification_market: Original Type 904 Carrera GTS production-road homologation family, selected 1964 four-cam street-car reference from Audrain Auto Museum's Begovich Collection. Porsche explicitly describes the original as designed for both road and racetrack; museum evidence documents genuine production road versions. Group all road outputs, equipment, years and individual chassis in one family. Dedicated works six/eight-cylinder versions and racing tunes are not selected or separately counted. Eight attributes use the museum's street-car account; RWD uses the FIA family index. Preserve its museum-listed 153 hp at 6900 rpm and 125 ft-lb at 5000 rpm without inventing a rating standard or converting units. This is not the 180 PS at 7200 rpm recognition-form tune, Revs #046's listed 180 HP at 7000 rpm, or the Porsche Museum eight-cylinder 240-hp car. Nominal 2.0 L only; no exact cc, engine-code suffix, compression, carburettor size, race mass, top speed or measured acceleration transferred from other configurations.
cars.summary: The 904 Carrera GTS combined mid-engine packaging and a GRP body bonded to a metal chassis in a limited-production road-and-race GT. Its enduring design and endurance-racing heritage give it an established place in Porsche history. Count the original production-road family once; the works engines, racing tunes and individual competition cars are not additional road entries.

sources.notes: Complete relevant collection description and specification panel read. Eight attributes map to this museum-held street-car reference: nominal 2.0 L/four-cam flat-four, listed 153 hp at 6900 rpm, 125 ft-lb at 5000 rpm, five-speed manual, mid-engine layout, bonded fibreglass body and coil springs. sources.publisher: Dr. Ing. h.c. F. Porsche AG
sources.title: 911 GTS press kit — The history, 904 Carrera GTS section, printed p.26
sources.notes: Downloaded 27-page PDF. Relevant history page index 25/printed p.26 individually rendered and read. Also read extracted overview paragraph at index 4; no whole 27-page visual audit. Explicitly describes F.A. Porsche's 904 as designed for road and racetrack, first Porsche GTS and first plastic-bodied Zuffenhausen sports car, unveiled 26 November 1963. Targa Florio win is programme context; no race performance, total-production figure, other GTS-model values or technical attribute imported.

sources.title: 1964 Porsche 904 Carrera GTS — collection car 904 046
sources.source_type: Original holding-museum history and engineering account
sources.notes: Complete relevant collection history and panel read after legacy collection-page redirect. Documents GRP body bonded to sheet-metal chassis rails, Heinkel production, racing heritage and lasting design, alongside body-thickness/weight variation, difficult access, driver-error sensitivity and gearbox limitations. Supplies admission context only. Its 180 HP at 7000 rpm and 1435-lb panel belongs to another museum reference; no value is assigned to the Audrain street car. Actual race results of #046 do not imply every production car raced. No claim that a linked video was watched.

facts.title: The first Porsche GTS
facts.explanation: Porsche's history identifies the 904 as the first GTS and its first plastic-bodied sports car, designed by Ferdinand Alexander Porsche for road and racetrack and unveiled on 26 November 1963. The 1964 Targa Florio victory belongs to the competition programme, not the operating record of every street example.
